overview: This area is the model zoo of the volforecast package: every forecasting model the pipeline can run, all speaking one contract so the walk-forward evaluation harness can treat a naive random walk and a graph attention network identically. A model is a class registered under a string name in MODEL_REGISTRY via the register_model decorator; volforecast.registry.ensure_registered() imports each module once so the decorators fire. All models inherit _BaseModel, which declares which feature layers the model needs (REQUIRED_LAYERS, default har_core), capability flags (supports_tuning, supports_fit_progress, supports_shap_selection, accepts_gpu_device, requires_sequences, and requires_graph on the graph models), plus joblib save/load. Prediction happens in log-RV space throughout, and essentially every trainable model optimizes QLIKE directly: LightGBM and XGBoost through hand-derived gradient and hessian custom objectives, the torch graph models through a shared _qlike_loss in gnn.py. The families: nine naive baselines that set the QLIKE floor (random walk, historical mean, rolling mean, median, EWMA, AR1, VIX-implied, ATM-IV-implied); the linear HAR family built on _BaseOLS with deterministic alpha grid tuning (its registration file har_family.py is missing from this restore); gradient boosting (lightgbm, lightgbm_dart, xgboost); a seven-model graph suite (gnn, ghar, gnnhar, dcrnn_har, stid, gsp_har, gnn_learned) built for careful attribution, where linear and edge-free controls nest the fancier models; and five ensembles or meta-models (lightgbm_bagged, lightgbm_calibrated, stacking_har_lgbm, regime_blend, blend). Optional pip extras gate the heavy dependencies: ml for boosted trees plus Optuna and SHAP, gpu for torch, graph for torch-geometric. Three import targets are confirmed missing in the restore (models/har_family.py, models/lstm.py, volforecast/config.py), so ensure_registered() would currently raise ImportError.

modules.role: Holds the three global registries (MODEL_REGISTRY, FEATURE_REGISTRY, GRAPH_REGISTRY) and the decorator functions that populate them, raising on duplicate names. ensure_registered() imports every feature, model and graph module exactly once so decorator-based registration fires; the gnn import is wrapped in try/except ImportError so CPU-only installs without torch still register the rest of the zoo. Note that it imports volforecast.models.har_family and volforecast.models.lstm, both absent from this restore, so ensure_registered() fails on this snapshot before reaching the graph model imports.

key_files.purpose: Decorator-based registries mapping model, feature-layer and graph-builder names to classes.

modules.role: The full model zoo: 24 registered model names across naive baselines, gradient boosting, graph neural models and ensembles, all inheriting the _BaseModel fit/predict contract defined in _base.py. Tabular models consume feature-layer DataFrames declared in REQUIRED_LAYERS; graph models set requires_graph = True and consume lists of per-date graph-dict snapshots built by gnn_adjacency.py from rolling realized correlations; sequence models would set requires_sequences = True and receive a SequenceTensor, but the LSTM file itself is missing from the restore. Nearly every trainable model optimizes QLIKE in log-RV space, so training loss equals the evaluation metric. The graph suite is engineered for attribution: ghar and gnnhar nest pooled HAR when the adjacency is zero, gsp_har nests QLIKE-HAR at initialization, and stid is an edges-ignored deflation control. Tuning is split by family: deterministic alpha grids for linear models (linear_tuning.py), Optuna for LightGBM, and multi-GPU Optuna harnesses for LSTM and GNN (lstm_tuning.py, gnn_tuning.py). The zoo feeds the pipeline runner and evaluation stack; gsvivs_classifier.py additionally turns the machinery into a precision-optimized trading signal on the GSVIVS01 index.

key_files.purpose: Re-exports MODEL_REGISTRY and register_model as the package's public surface.
_BaseModel root contract (save/load, capability flags, tune_and_fit hook), _BaseOLS for the linear HAR family, and the temporal_holdout_split helper.
Nine zero-or-minimal-parameter baselines that set the QLIKE floor, from random walk to VIX-implied and per-symbol ATM-IV-implied forecasts.
Deterministic Optuna-free alpha and l1_ratio grid search for ridge, lasso and elasticnet HAR variants on inner expanding-window CV.
LightGBM regressor with custom QLIKE objective, Optuna tuning, TreeSHAP selection, plus the lightgbm_dart dropout variant.
XGBoost twin of the LightGBM model with the same QLIKE custom objective, an optional mse objective, and a residual-on-base-model mode.
lightgbm_bagged K-seed bagging ensemble that averages members in log-RV space to shrink the seed-noise envelope.
lightgbm_calibrated: post-hoc affine recalibration learned on a purged temporal holdout to fix QLIKE level bias.
stacking_har_lgbm: Ridge meta-learner over HAR and LightGBM predictions to combine discrimination with calibrated levels.
regime_blend: HAR plus LightGBM blend with regime-dependent weights switched on a log_rv_w percentile threshold.
Generic prediction-level blend of registry sub-models with weights calibrated on a temporal holdout per BlendConfig.
gnn: GATv2 graph attention network over per-date correlation graph snapshots, plus the shared QLIKE loss and device helpers used by all torch graph models.
Builds cached sparse edge tensors from rolling realized correlation with a causal window and absolute-correlation threshold.
ghar: pooled-OLS linear graph HAR whose zero-adjacency case recovers pooled HAR exactly, isolating the graph's contribution.
gnnhar: nonlinear one-hop GCN spillover channel plus linear HAR readout with per-asset intercepts and multi-seed prediction averaging.
dcrnn_har: diffusion-convolutional GRU (Li et al. 2018) over sequences of graph snapshots with a jointly trained HAR skip channel.
stid: per-node identity embedding plus MLP deflation control that runs the graph harness while ignoring edges entirely.
gsp_har: magnetic Laplacian spectral filter model (Chi, Gao and Wang 2024) with per-refit-block eigendecomposition caching.
gnn_learned: MTGNN-style learned directed adjacency with row-wise top-k sparsification feeding a one-hop GCN body.
Optuna multi-GPU tuning harness for the GATv2 and GNNHAR search spaces, coordinated via JournalStorage.
Optuna multi-GPU tuning harness for the LSTM sequence model (whose lstm.py implementation is missing from the restore).
Unregistered LightGBM binary classifier producing a precision-optimized short signal on GSVIVS01 index drawdowns.

claims.text: Every model self-registers under a string name into MODEL_REGISTRY through the register_model class decorator, so the pipeline can instantiate any of the 24 names registered across the models package from configuration alone.
claims.quote: MODEL_REGISTRY[name] = cls

claims.text: The registry imports the GNN module inside a try/except ImportError so a CPU-only install without torch still registers the rest of the model zoo, with torch_geometric deferred until GNN construction.

All models inherit _BaseModel, which declares the feature layers a model needs (default har_core), capability flags for tuning, fit progress, TreeSHAP selection and GPU device, and joblib save/load, giving every family one shared fit/predict contract.

claims.text: Linear HAR-family models share _BaseOLS, which restricts the design matrix to a declared feature list, masks NaN rows, drops all-NaN columns, and exposes alpha and l1_ratio grid hooks for ridge, lasso and elasticnet variants.

class _BaseOLS(_BaseModel):
    """OLS/regularized regression models (HAR family)."""

claims.text: LightGBM trains directly on the QLIKE loss in log-RV space through a custom objective with analytic gradient 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred) and hessian exp(y_true - y_pred), so trees split to minimize the vol forecaster's actual evaluation metric.
claims.quote:
Log-space QLIKE: L = exp(y_true - y_pred) - (y_true - y_pred) - 1
    gradient (dL/dy_pred) = 1 - exp(y_true - y_pred)
    hessian  (d²L/dy_pred²) = exp(y_true - y_pred)

claims.text: The lightgbm model consumes six feature layers (har_core, asymmetry, noise_robust, options, calendar, tree_expansion) and is the most capable model in the zoo, with Optuna tuning, fit progress callbacks, TreeSHAP feature selection and GPU device selection all enabled.
claims.quote:
REQUIRED_LAYERS = [
        "har_core",
        "asymmetry",
        "noise_robust",
        "options",
        "calendar",
        "tree_expansion",
    ]

claims.text: lightgbm_dart subclasses the LightGBM model with DART dropout regularization to produce less overconfident volatility predictions, carrying its own shallower default parameter set.

xgboost is a parallel gradient-boosted tree implementation with the same QLIKE custom objective and the same six required feature layers, letting the pipeline cross-check LightGBM results against an independent boosting library.

Nine naive baselines (random_walk alias same_day_rv, historical_mean, rolling_mean, median_rv, ewma, ar1, vix_implied, atm_iv_implied) implement the same fit/predict interface with zero or minimal training and set the QLIKE floor any useful model must beat.
claims.quote:
These implement the fit/predict interface but require no training or minimal
training (just computing a mean). They provide a floor for QLIKE comparison:
any useful model must beat these.

claims.text: The ewma baseline is the RiskMetrics estimator with lambda 0.94, recursively updating ewma_t = lambda * ewma_{t-1} + (1 - lambda) * log_rv_{t-1} through the test period.
claims.quote:
Uses lambda=0.94 (JP Morgan 1996 standard). At each test point, the
    forecast is: ewma_t = lambda * ewma_{t-1} + (1 - lambda) * log_rv_{t-1}.

claims.text: vix_implied converts the option market's VIX quote straight into a daily variance forecast via log_rv = 2*log(VIX/100) - log(252), a zero-parameter benchmark of implied against realized volatility.
claims.quote: The forecast: log_rv = 2*log(VIX/100) - log(252).

claims.text: The gnn model treats each trading date as one graph snapshot with symbols as nodes and rolling-correlation edges, learning with GATv2 attention how volatility spills across the asset network rather than through time.
claims.quote:
Operates on graph snapshots: each date = one graph with N nodes
    (symbols) and edges from rolling correlation. Integrates with the

claims.text: gnnhar implements the nonlinear graph HAR of Zhang, Pu, Cucuringu and Dong 2025: a GCN spillover channel with no self-loops plus a linear HAR channel, defaulting to the paper's hidden dimension of 9.
claims.quote: description = "GNNHAR: no-self-loop GCN spillover channel + linear HAR channel"

claims.text: stid is a deliberate deflation control, per-node identity embeddings plus an MLP that ignores graph edges, so if it matches gnnhar the honest conclusion is that pooling plus asset identity suffices, not that spillovers matter.
claims.quote:
consuming the same graph-dict harness but ignoring edges entirely. If STID
matches GNNHAR, the honest conclusion is "pooling + asset identity suffices",
not "spillovers matter".

claims.text: gsp_har applies a learnable complex spectral filter in the eigenbasis of a magnetic Laplacian (Chi, Gao and Wang 2024) on top of a linear HAR channel, with the filter initialized to zero so the model nests QLIKE-HAR at initialization.
claims.quote: description = "GSP-HAR: magnetic Laplacian spectral filter + linear HAR channel"

claims.text: gnn_learned ignores the input graph entirely and learns a directed sparse adjacency end-to-end from node embeddings using the MTGNN graph-learning layer with row-wise top-k sparsification.
claims.quote: description = "GNN learned adjacency: MTGNN graph-learning + one-hop GCN body"

claims.text: lightgbm_bagged averages K seed-varied LightGBM fits because the trial-047 reseed study measured a 6.6 bps seed envelope at h=1, meaning single-seed feature-engineering deltas under roughly 10 bps are indistinguishable from seed noise.
claims.quote:
The trial-047 reseed baseline measured a 6.6 bps seed envelope at h=1
    on the trial-036 champion spec. Single-seed numbers are inside this noise
    floor, so feature-engineering deltas <~10 bps cannot be distinguished

claims.text: regime_blend encodes the 2026-05-27 research finding that the optimal HAR weight in a HAR plus LightGBM blend is massively regime-dependent at h=22: about 0.05 in low-vol regimes where LightGBM dominates but about 0.80 in high-vol regimes where HAR dominates.
claims.quote:
Research finding (2026-05-27): Optimal blend weight is massively
regime-dependent at h=22:
  - Low-vol: LightGBM dominates (optimal HAR weight ~0.05)
  - High-vol: HAR dominates (optimal HAR weight ~0.80)

glossary.definition: Quasi-likelihood loss for variance forecasts; in log-RV space L = exp(y_true - y_pred) - (y_true - y_pred) - 1, which penalizes under-predicting volatility more than over-predicting it.
Heterogeneous autoregressive model: regresses future realized volatility on daily, weekly and monthly RV lags, the standard linear benchmark in vol forecasting.
Global dict mapping model name strings to model classes, populated by the register_model decorator when ensure_registered() imports the model modules.
Class flag telling the pipeline runner to dispatch per-date graph snapshots (node features plus edge tensors) instead of tabular features to this model.
The per-symbol history tensor fed to sequence-first models when requires_sequences is True, replacing the tabular DataFrame path in the runner.
Exponentially weighted moving average of log-RV with lambda 0.94, the 1996 JP Morgan RiskMetrics standard, used here as a naive baseline.
Graph attention convolution that learns attention weights over neighboring assets; the gnn model stacks two GATv2Conv layers with multi-head attention.
A complex-valued graph Laplacian whose phase encodes edge direction, giving gsp_har a spectral basis for directed volatility spillover graphs.
The systematic gap by which option-implied volatility exceeds subsequently realized volatility, making IV a biased but informative RV predictor.
The spread of QLIKE scores across retrainings that differ only in random seed; measured at 6.6 bps at h=1, it sets the noise floor for judging feature changes.
A baseline deliberately stripped of the mechanism under test (for stid, the graph edges) so that gains claimed for that mechanism can be attributed honestly.
